questions.question_text: One algorithm has time complexity $O(n^2)$ and another has $\Theta(n \log n)$. Which one is always asymptotically better for large input sizes?
options: Cannot be determined without constant factors
questions.answer: Asymptotically, as $n$ grows very large, $n \log n$ grows much slower than $n^2$. Thus, $\Theta(n \log n)$ represents a better complexity class than $O(n^2)$.

questions.question_text: If an algorithm has time complexity $O(n^2)$, There exists a constant time c such that, which of the following are true?
options: It takes at most $c \cdot n^2$ time
questions.answer: Big-O notation represents an asymptotic upper bound. By definition, $f(n) = O(g(n))$ implies $f(n) \le c \cdot g(n)$ for some positive constant $c$ and sufficiently large $n$. Thus, it takes at most $c \cdot n^2$ time.

questions.question_text: Which of the following are true about Abstract Data Types?
options: ADTs hide implementation details from the user
ADTs only include primitive data types
Stack and Queue are examples of ADTs
ADTs are defined by the operations performed on them
questions.answer:
A, C and D are true.
- A is correct because abstraction hides the implementation details from the client.
- B is incorrect because ADTs can include both primitive and non-primitive custom data models.
- C is correct as Stack and Queue are standard examples of ADTs.
- D is correct as ADTs are specified strictly in terms of their operations and behaviors.
